extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing a Journal of Open Source Software (JOSS) paper using GitHub and CircleCI (developers packaging paper.md and paper.bib for submission)
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and checklist for preparing, validating, and optionally deploying a JOSS submission using a GitHub repository and CircleCI; focuses on required files, CI configuration, validation steps, and deployment prerequisites. Targets authors who will produce paper.md and paper.bib and want automated validation and PDF preview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper file layout
rubrics_metrics.description: The submission must include a folder named `paper` containing a `paper.md` and a matching `paper.bib`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repository should have structure: paper/ paper.md paper.bib. An example paper is provided in the paper folder. This is the canonical location the CI workflow expects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic validation of paper.md and paper.bib
rubrics_metrics.description: The template validates `paper.md` and `paper.bib` for programmatic properties such as length and formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validation is automated in CI and checks machine-verifiable items (e.g., formatting, bibliography structure, length). The template will NOT check 'human' elements like whether your summary is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use JOSS/whedon templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper must use the JOSS template served by `whedon`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This repository uses the JOSS template; the build will render the paper with JOSS templates. Ensure the paper content conforms to the template expectations (the example in `paper/` shows the expected format).

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF generation with JOSS branding
rubrics_metrics.description: The CI build will generate a PDF using the JOSS templates and logo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CircleCI job builds a PDF using the JOSS templates and logo so you can preview the final rendered submission. The template also supports alternate builder containers (e.g., openbases/openbases-pdf) if you want local rendering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required CI configuration files
rubrics_metrics.description: To run builds and validation in CircleCI, include a `.circleci/config.yml` (and optionally `.circleci/template.html` for GitHub Pages deployment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hidden folder `.circleci/config.yml` contains the workflow steps for clone, validation, build, and optional deploy. You only need `.circleci/config.yml` and `.circleci/template.html` for the CI integration to work.

rubrics_metrics.name: CI workflow steps
rubrics_metrics.description: The CircleCI workflow should perform: clone of the repository, validation of `paper.md` and `paper.bib` (per the template criteria), build the PDF, and optionally push to GitHub Pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provided `.circleci/config.yml` implements these steps by default. You can edit the config to change behavior, add tests, filters, or additional deployment steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: GitHub Pages deployment prerequisites (machine user & deploy key)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to push the rendered PDF back to GitHub Pages, you must create a machine user with write access and provide a deploy key with write permissions to CircleCI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: create a second GitHub account (machine user) with a different email, add it as a collaborator with push access, accept the invitation, log into CircleCI as the machine user, 'Follow Project', then in Project Settings -> 'Checkout SSH keys' click 'Authorize with GitHub' and add the machine user's SSH key ('Add user key'). CircleCI generates read-only deploy keys by default; you need this machine user key so CircleCI can push.

rubrics_metrics.name: CircleCI environment variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Set required environment variables in CircleCI project settings: `GITHUB_USER`, `GITHUB_EMAIL`, `OPENBASES_VALIDATE_ARGS`, and `OPENBASES_PAPER_ARGS`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: `GITHUB_USER` and `GITHUB_EMAIL` should be the machine user's GitHub account. `OPENBASES_VALIDATE_ARGS` passes additional arguments to openbases validation (ob-validate). `OPENBASES_PAPER_ARGS` defines extra argument pairs to pass into the openbases/openbases-pdf container entrypoint; these are interpolated into the entrypoint command.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local validation using openbases Docker images
rubrics_metrics.description: You can run validations locally using the `openbases/openbases` Docker image, and generate PDFs locally with `openbases/openbases-pdf`.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the Docker images avoids needing CI for validation. The `openbases/openbases-pdf` builder can also be used to render PDFs locally if you want to preview without CI. The `openbases/builder-pdf` repo provides a template that uses a different icon instead of the JOSS logo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customization of build and template
rubrics_metrics.description: You may customize the CircleCI config and `template.html` used for rendering; the CircleCI configuration file and template are fully editable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Customizations can range from trivial text changes to adding steps or filters in the workflow. `template.html` is populated with environment variables and can be modified or replaced to change the rendered HTML/PDF. For pull requests, configure CircleCI filters if you want different behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the template (what it does not do)
rubrics_metrics.description: The template will not submit the paper to JOSS on your behalf and will not verify subjective/human aspects of the submission (e.g., completeness of summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must still submit the validated PDF through JOSS's submission process. The template focuses on machine-checkable aspects (formatting, bibliographic validity, length) and CI-driven build/deploy functionality.
